requirements.original: The module definitions part specifies the top-level definitions of the module and may import visible identifiers from other modules.
requirements.canonical: The module definitions part MAY import visible identifiers from other modules.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- The module definitions part specifies the top-level definitions of the module and may import visible identifiers from other modules.

requirements.original: Every definition can be associated with attributes using the with statement defined in clause 27.
requirements.canonical: Every module definition MAY be associated with attributes using the `with` statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- Every definition can be associated with attributes using the with statement defined in clause 27.

requirements.original: Visible module definitions may be imported by other modules.
requirements.canonical: A visible module definition MAY be imported by other modules.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- Visible module definitions may be imported by other modules.

requirements.original: { [ Visibility ] ( TypeDef | ConstDef | TemplateDef | ModuleParDef | FunctionDef | SignatureDef | TestcaseDef | AltstepDef | ImportDef | GroupDef | ExtFunctionDef | FriendDef | ModuleControlDef ) [ WithStatement ] [ ";" ] }+
requirements.canonical: The module definitions part IS a sequence of one or more module definitions, each consisting of an optional Visibility, one of TypeDef, ConstDef, TemplateDef, ModuleParDef, FunctionDef, SignatureDef, TestcaseDef, AltstepDef, ImportDef, GroupDef, ExtFunctionDef, FriendDef or ModuleControlDef, an optional WithStatement and an optional ";".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- { [ Visibility ] ( TypeDef | ConstDef | TemplateDef | ModuleParDef | FunctionDef | SignatureDef | TestcaseDef | AltstepDef | ImportDef | GroupDef | ExtFunctionDef | FriendDef | ModuleControlDef ) [ WithStatement ] [ ";" ] }+

requirements.original: Definitions in the module definitions part may be made in any order.
requirements.canonical: Definitions in the module definitions part MAY be made in any order.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- Definitions in the module definitions part may be made in any order.

requirements.original: A definition shall be evaluated latest before the first reference to it.
requirements.canonical: A module definition SHALL be evaluated at the latest before the first reference to it.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- A definition shall be evaluated latest before the first reference to it.

requirements.original: Such definitions, i.e. top-level definitions outside of other scope units, are globally visible within the module.
requirements.canonical: A top-level module definition outside of other scope units IS globally visible within the module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- Such definitions, i.e. top-level definitions outside of other scope units, are globally visible within the module.

requirements.original: They may be used elsewhere in the module.
requirements.canonical: A top-level module definition MAY be used elsewhere in the module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- They may be used elsewhere in the module.

requirements.original: This includes identifiers imported from other modules. Such definitions, i.e. top-level definitions outside of other scope units, are globally visible within the module.
requirements.canonical: An identifier imported from another module IS globally visible within the importing module and MAY be used elsewhere in it.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- This includes identifiers imported from other modules. Such definitions, i.e. top-level definitions outside of other scope units, are globally visible within the module.

requirements.original: Declarations of dynamic language elements such as variables or timers shall only be made in test cases, functions, altsteps or component types.
requirements.canonical: A declaration of a dynamic language element, such as a variable or a timer, SHALL only be made in a test case, function, altstep or component type.

readings: Variables and timers SHALL only be declared in test cases, functions, altsteps or component types (list is exhaustive).
Variables and timers SHALL only be declared in test cases, functions, altsteps, component types and the module control part.
ambiguity.issue: The list omits the module control part, in which variables and timers are allowed (clause 26); the literal list is kept in the canonical text, the control part is considered allowed by clause 26.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- Declarations of dynamic language elements such as variables or timers shall only be made in test cases, functions, altsteps or component types.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 does not support the declaration of variables in the module definitions part, i.e. global variables cannot be defined in TTCN-3.
requirements.canonical: A variable SHALL NOT be declared in the module definitions part (TTCN-3 has no global variables).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- TTCN-3 does not support the declaration of variables in the module definitions part, i.e. global variables cannot be defined in TTCN-3.

requirements.original: However, variables defined in a test component type may be used by all test cases, functions, etc. running on components of that component type.
requirements.canonical: A component variable MAY be used by all test cases, functions and altsteps running on a component of that component type.

improper_terms.used: variables defined in a test component type

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.0 -- However, variables defined in a test component type may be used by all test cases, functions, etc. running on components of that component type.

requirements.original: Module parameters do not change during test execution.
requirements.canonical: The value of a module parameter IS NOT changed during test execution.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- Module parameters do not change during test execution.

requirements.original: They can be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters, and in template definitions, but not within type definitions.
requirements.canonical: A module parameter MAY be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters and in template definitions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- They can be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters, and in template definitions, but not within type definitions.

requirements.original: They can be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters, and in template definitions, but not within type definitions.
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL NOT be used within a type definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- They can be used on the right hand side of assignments, in expressions, in actual parameters, and in template definitions, but not within type definitions.

requirements.original: [ Visibility ] modulepar [ TemplateModifier ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] { Identifier [ ":=" TemplateBody ] "," } Identifier [ ":=" TemplateBody ] ";"
requirements.canonical: A module parameter declaration has the syntax [Visibility] `modulepar` [TemplateModifier] [TypeOrNestedTypeDef] Identifier [":=" TemplateBody] {"," Identifier [":=" TemplateBody]} ";".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- [ Visibility ] modulepar [ TemplateModifier ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] { Identifier [ ":=" TemplateBody ] "," } Identifier [ ":=" TemplateBody ] ";"

requirements.original: Module parameters behave as global constants or unparameterized templates at runtime.
requirements.canonical: A module parameter behaves at runtime as a global constant or as an unparameterized template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- Module parameters behave as global constants or unparameterized templates at runtime.

requirements.original: For module parameterization, TTCN-3 only supports value parameterization which has to be resolved static at start of runtime.
requirements.canonical: Module parameterization IS restricted to value parameterization.

readings: Module parameters are only supported as static (value) parameterization resolved at start of runtime, which includes template module parameters.
Module parameters SHALL only be values, not templates.
ambiguity.issue: 'value parameterization' conflicts with template module parameters allowed by s001/s004; the reading 'static parameterization (values and templates) resolved at start of runtime' is chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- For module parameterization, TTCN-3 only supports value parameterization which has to be resolved static at start of runtime.

requirements.original: For module parameterization, TTCN-3 only supports value parameterization which has to be resolved static at start of runtime.
requirements.canonical: The actual values of module parameters SHALL be resolved statically at the start of runtime.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- For module parameterization, TTCN-3 only supports value parameterization which has to be resolved static at start of runtime.

requirements.original: It is allowed to specify a default value or template for each module parameter as part of the modulepar declaration.
requirements.canonical: A module parameter declaration MAY specify a default value or template for the module parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- It is allowed to specify a default value or template for each module parameter as part of the modulepar declaration.

requirements.original: If the test system does not provide an actual runtime value or template for a module parameter, the given default value or template shall be used during test execution, otherwise the actual value or template provided by the test system.
requirements.canonical: If the test system does not provide an actual runtime value or template for a module parameter, the default value or template given in the declaration SHALL be used during test execution.
requirements.condition: the test system does not provide a value or template for the module parameter
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- If the test system does not provide an actual runtime value or template for a module parameter, the given default value or template shall be used during test execution, otherwise the actual value or template provided by the test system.

requirements.original: If the test system does not provide an actual runtime value or template for a module parameter, the given default value or template shall be used during test execution, otherwise the actual value or template provided by the test system.
requirements.canonical: If the test system provides an actual value or template for a module parameter, that actual value or template SHALL be used during test execution instead of the default.
requirements.condition: the test system provides a value or template for the module parameter
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- If the test system does not provide an actual runtime value or template for a module parameter, the given default value or template shall be used during test execution, otherwise the actual value or template provided by the test system.

requirements.original: The type of the module parameter is either provided explicitly or implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing specified in the clause 6.5.
requirements.canonical: The type of a module parameter IS either given explicitly or determined implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- The type of the module parameter is either provided explicitly or implicitly according to the rules for automatic typing specified in the clause 6.5.

requirements.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.
requirements.canonical: When automatic typing is used for a module parameter, the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part of the declaration IS omitted.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax block and restriction i) use 'TypeOrNestedTypeDef'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.

requirements.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.
requirements.canonical: When automatic typing is used for a module parameter, the type of the module parameter IS the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.

requirements.original: Visible module parameters can be imported.
requirements.canonical: A visible module parameter MAY be imported.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- Visible module parameters can be imported.

requirements.original: Optional fields of record and set module parameters or module parameter fields can be initialized explicitly or implicitly.
requirements.canonical: An optional field of a record or set module parameter or module parameter field MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- Optional fields of record and set module parameters or module parameter fields can be initialized explicitly or implicitly.

requirements.original: For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a module parameter or a module parameter field, an optional attribute with the value "implicit omit" (see clause 27.7) shall be associated with it either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism (see clause 27.1.1).
requirements.canonical: For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a module parameter or module parameter field, an `optional` attribute with the value "implicit omit" SHALL be associated with it, either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism.
requirements.condition: the optional fields are to be initialized implicitly
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- For implicit initialization of the optional fields of a module parameter or a module parameter field, an optional attribute with the value "implicit omit" (see clause 27.7) shall be associated with it either directly or via the attribute distribution (scoping) mechanism (see clause 27.1.1).

requirements.original: a) During test execution module parameters shall not be used as target of assignments or as actual out or inout parameters.
requirements.canonical: During test execution a module parameter SHALL NOT be used as the target of an assignment.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- a) During test execution module parameters shall not be used as target of assignments or as actual out or inout parameters.

requirements.original: a) During test execution module parameters shall not be used as target of assignments or as actual out or inout parameters.
requirements.canonical: During test execution a module parameter SHALL NOT be used as an actual `out` or `inout` parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- a) During test execution module parameters shall not be used as target of assignments or as actual out or inout parameters.

requirements.original: b) Module parameters shall not be of port, default, timer or component type and shall not be of a structured type that contains a sub-element of port or timer type at any level of nesting.
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL NOT be of port, default, timer or component type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- b) Module parameters shall not be of port, default, timer or component type and shall not be of a structured type that contains a sub-element of port or timer type at any level of nesting.

requirements.original: b) Module parameters shall not be of port, default, timer or component type and shall not be of a structured type that contains a sub-element of port or timer type at any level of nesting.
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL NOT be of a structured type that contains a sub-element of port or timer type at any level of nesting.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- b) Module parameters shall not be of port, default, timer or component type and shall not be of a structured type that contains a sub-element of port or timer type at any level of nesting.

requirements.original: c) A module parameter shall only be of type address if the address type is explicitly defined within the associated module.
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL only be of the address type if the address type is explicitly defined within the module containing the module parameter declaration.

readings: The address type SHALL be defined in the module that declares the module parameter.
The address type SHALL be defined in, or be visible (e.g. imported) in, the module associated with the module parameter.
ambiguity.issue: 'explicitly defined within the associated module' does not say whether an imported address type definition suffices; the literal reading is chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- c) A module parameter shall only be of type address if the address type is explicitly defined within the associated module.

requirements.original: d) Module parameters shall be declared within the module definition part only.
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL be declared only within the module definitions part.

ambiguity.issue: Clause 8.2 uses the name 'module definitions part'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- d) Module parameters shall be declared within the module definition part only.

requirements.original: e) More than one occurrence of module parameters declaration is allowed but each parameter shall be declared only once (i.e. redefinition of the module parameter is not allowed).
requirements.canonical: A module MAY contain more than one module parameter declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- e) More than one occurrence of module parameters declaration is allowed but each parameter shall be declared only once (i.e. redefinition of the module parameter is not allowed).

requirements.original: e) More than one occurrence of module parameters declaration is allowed but each parameter shall be declared only once (i.e. redefinition of the module parameter is not allowed).
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL be declared only once, i.e. a module parameter SHALL NOT be redefined.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- e) More than one occurrence of module parameters declaration is allowed but each parameter shall be declared only once (i.e. redefinition of the module parameter is not allowed).

requirements.original: f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody of a module parameter SHALL respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.

requirements.original: f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody of a module parameter SHALL be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.

requirements.original: f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody of a module parameter SHALL conform to the TemplateModifier of the declaration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.

requirements.original: If no TemplateModifier is present, the TemplateBody shall resolve to a value. f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.
requirements.canonical: If no TemplateModifier is present in a module parameter declaration, the TemplateBody SHALL resolve to a value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- If no TemplateModifier is present, the TemplateBody shall resolve to a value. f) The TemplateBody of a module parameter shall respect the limitations given in clause 16.1.4. and shall be compatible with the TypeOrNestedTypeDef of the declaration and conform to the given TemplateModifier.

requirements.original: g) Module parameters shall not be used in type or array definitions.
requirements.canonical: A module parameter SHALL NOT be used in a type definition or array definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- g) Module parameters shall not be used in type or array definitions.

requirements.original: h) All sub-elements of component or default type of a default value of a module parameter shall be initialized with the special value null.
requirements.canonical: Every sub-element of component or default type of the default value of a module parameter SHALL be initialized with the special value `null`.

readings: Sub-elements of component or default type in the default value SHALL be `null`.
This rule implies that module parameters of structured types with component or default sub-elements are allowed, which restriction b) does not forbid; only the default must use `null`.
ambiguity.issue: Restriction b) forbids top-level component and default types but only forbids port/timer sub-elements; the first reading is chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- h) All sub-elements of component or default type of a default value of a module parameter shall be initialized with the special value null.

requirements.original: i) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a module parameter declaration, the assignment part ":=" TemplateBody SHALL be present.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.2.1 -- i) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.
